person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the structural determinants of ion selectivity in channelrhodopsin pores, and the inhibitory tools they make possible
span.quote: Because optogenetic control of behavior has not yet been demonstrated with chloride channelrhodopsins, and to test further integrative ideas regarding pore function from structural considerations as shown here, we sought to design and test the next generation of enhanced chloride channels (iC++ and SwiChR++). Along the way, we provide the initial test of the hypothesis that light-activated channels will be more efficient tools than pumps for optogenetic neuronal inhibition at the cellular level, demonstrate the initial utility of light-gated chloride channels in controlling behavior in freely moving animals, and reveal key principles regarding the functional selectivity of light-gated ion channel pores.

span.label: whether an electrostatic model of the pore can be pushed further to build chloride channels usable for behavioural inhibition
span.quote: Engineered channels indeed became chloride selective, reversing near −65 mV and enabling a new kind of optogenetic inhibition; however, these first-generation chloride-conducting channels displayed small photocurrents and were not tested for optogenetic inhibition of behavior.

span.label: builds enhanced chloride-conducting channelrhodopsins with 15-fold larger photocurrents, demonstrates the first behavioural control with them, and shows inhibition works by shunting rather than hyperpolarisation
span.quote: Here we report the validation and further development of the channelrhodopsin pore model via crystal structure-guided engineering of next-generation light-activated chloride channels (iC++) and a bistable variant (SwiChR++) with net photocurrents increased more than 15-fold under physiological conditions, reversal potential further decreased by another ∼15 mV, inhibition of spiking faithfully tracking chloride gradients and intrinsic cell properties, strong expression in vivo, and the initial microbial opsin channel-inhibitor–based control of freely moving behavior.

span.label: method
span.quote: Here we describe the engineering of enhanced light-gated chloride channels (iC++ and SwiChR++) by structure-guided modification of ion selectivity, show improved efficiency for optical inhibition of neurons with these proteins, and demonstrate initial behavioral control in freely moving mammals.

span.label: channelrhodopsin ion selectivity
span.quote: This paper tests the hypothesis that selectivity of channelrhodopsins is determined by surface potential of the pore region: Cations are conducted by a negatively charged pore, and chloride ions are conducted by a pore that has neutral and positively charged residues.

span.label: system-or-tool-building
span.quote: In confirming this hypothesis and applying the resulting principles, we engineer improved chloride-conducting channels with higher chloride selectivity and conductivity.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Ions are selected by electrostatic interaction with the charged residues lining the pore, so replacing glutamates with neutral/basic residues flips selectivity from cations to chloride
span.quote: The enhancements comprising iC++ support the model of channelrhodopsin selectivity ( 8 ) in which ions are selected primarily by electrostatic interactions between pore and ions.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Protonation of basic pore residues under acidic conditions creates favourable electrostatics for chloride, which is why the earlier iC1C2 conducted chloride better at low pH
span.quote: We hypothesized that this pH dependency resulted from basic residues in the pore region of iC1C2, with higher probability of protonation under acidic conditions that established favorable electrostatic interactions for chloride ions.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Inhibition works by shunting: opening the chloride conductance drops input resistance and shunts excitatory input, rather than by hyperpolarizing the cell
span.quote: The main mechanism of this efficient inhibition from iC++ is likely via shunting inhibition, because the V rev of iC++ lies between the V AP and V rest (revealing that the inhibition is not driven by strong hyperpolarization).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Reduced input resistance lowers excitability in the same way endogenous GABA-A chloride channels do
span.quote: Reduction in R in through iC++ activation will reduce excitability, just as seen with endogenous chloride-conducting channels such as GABA A receptors, providing efficient inhibition via shunting of excitatory inputs ( 20 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The longer arginine side chain substituted at position 134 sterically blocks channel closure, producing the dark leak current and low input resistance of the E83X mutants
span.quote: Indeed, the longer arginine side chain (compared with histidine) could, in principle, interfere with channel closure of iC1C2-E83X mutants, increasing leak currents in the dark and leading to reduced R in for these otherwise interesting E83 variants.

span.label: ions are selected by electrostatic interaction with the pore, so replacing negatively charged residues with neutral or positive ones flips the channel from cation- to anion-conducting
span.quote: iC1C2 and iC++ are highly engineered (9 and 10 residues were replaced, respectively) variants of the cation-selective parental construct C1C2, with mutations chosen for the predicted ability to alter the electrostatic potential

span.label: inhibition works by shunting excitatory input, as endogenous chloride channels do, rather than by hyperpolarising the cell
span.quote: through iC++ activation will reduce excitability, just as seen with endogenous chloride-conducting channels such as GABA A receptors, providing efficient inhibition via shunting of excitatory inputs

span.label: a structural argument diagnosed the leak: a longer arginine side chain where wild type has histidine could block channel closure, and reverting it restored input resistance
span.quote: Because both E83 and R134 were shown to be inner pore-gate residues in the C1C2 structure ( 7 ), we considered the possibility that a disruptive interaction had been created here by joint mutation at these two residues. Indeed, the longer arginine side chain (compared with histidine) could, in principle, interfere with channel closure of iC1C2-E83X mutants, increasing leak currents in the dark and leading to reduced R in for these otherwise interesting E83 variants.

span.label: the pH dependence of the first-generation channel was traced to protonatable pore residues and removed by further substitution
span.quote: We hypothesized that this pH dependency resulted from basic residues in the pore region of iC1C2, with higher probability of protonation under acidic conditions that established favorable electrostatic interactions for chloride ions. By removing more negatively charged residues from the ion-conducting pore and introducing two arginines, we increased the chloride selectivity and also strongly reduced the pH dependency of chloride conductivity.

span.label: channels follow the cell's own chloride gradient while pumps move ions unidirectionally regardless of it
span.quote: For the same reason, iC++ currents will mirror the physiological effects of endogenous open chloride channels more precisely

span.label: Spike inhibition by iC++ is not absolute: with intracellular chloride above the physiological range it can be partially overcome by very strong current injection.
span.quote: When APs were evoked by pulsed current injections, nearly complete spike inhibition was observed even with intracellular chloride elevated beyond the typical physiological range of 4–20 mM, although the inhibition in such cases could be partially overcome with extremely strong (0.8-nA) current injections ( SI Appendix , Fig. S3 ).

span.label: iC++ is not presented as universally superior; the choice between channel and pump depends on the preparation and hypothesis.
span.quote: iC++ and related channels ( 33 ) represent a different class of optogenetic tool, which, like any reagent in biology, should be selected based on suitability for preparation and hypothesis.

span.label: because channels follow physiological gradients, which differ by cell type, subcellular region, developmental stage and pathology, the tool can even excite under some conditions
span.quote: In addition, microbial opsin pump currents will not show the influence of ion gradients reported here for channels; such gradients can differ across cell types, subcellular regions, developmental stages, and pathological states ( 12 – 15 , 30 ), even giving rise to excitation under some conditions.

span.label: pumps hyperpolarise far beyond physiological levels and destabilise membrane properties
span.quote: Although optogenetic inhibitory pumps display more extreme V rev than the inhibitory channels described here, the pumps can hyperpolarize cells far beyond physiological levels, causing unstable membrane properties

span.label: lowering pump light intensity fixes that but shrinks the inhibited tissue volume, with no clean solution
span.quote: This effect can be reduced by lowering light intensity, although this strategy also severely reduces the volume of tissue inhibited by the pumps, which are less light sensitive than channels and, unlike the channels, cannot be converted to a more light-sensitive bistable step-function form.

span.label: the tool is explicitly not universally better - it must be chosen for the preparation and the hypothesis
span.quote: iC++ and related channels ( 33 ) represent a different class of optogenetic tool, which, like any reagent in biology, should be selected based on suitability for preparation and hypothesis.

span.label: in both behavioural assays the three opsins performed equivalently, so the assays do not resolve the cellular differences the paper establishes
span.quote: Under these experimental conditions, each opsin was equally effective in driving real-time place aversion (two-way repeated-measures ANOVA, no effect of group or group × light power interaction, P > 0.474).

span.label: a crystal structure and an electrostatic potential calculation, used as the design specification for a behavioural tool
span.quote: The design and functional features of these next-generation chloride-conducting channelrhodopsins provide both chronic and acute timescale tools for reversible optogenetic inhibition, confirm fundamental predictions of the ion selectivity model

span.label: shunting inhibition by GABA-A receptors, used as the model for how the engineered channel acts
span.quote: through iC++ activation will reduce excitability, just as seen with endogenous chloride-conducting channels such as GABA A receptors, providing efficient inhibition via shunting of excitatory inputs

span.label: optogenetic inhibition is not one thing: a chloride CHANNEL shunts along the cell's own gradient, a chloride PUMP moves ions against it, and the two differ in efficiency, stability and dependence on the preparation
span.quote: We observed that, because of stronger shunting, the chloride channel iC++ inhibited APs more efficiently than the chloride pump eNpHR3.0.

span.label: inhibitory is a property of the tool IN A PREPARATION, not of the tool - the same channel can excite where the chloride gradient runs the other way
span.quote: In addition, microbial opsin pump currents will not show the influence of ion gradients reported here for channels; such gradients can differ across cell types, subcellular regions, developmental stages, and pathological states ( 12 – 15 , 30 ), even giving rise to excitation under some conditions.

span.label: the electrostatic pore model is treated as a predictive hypothesis, and each round of engineering is described as a test of it rather than as an application
span.quote: The design and functional features of these next-generation chloride-conducting channelrhodopsins provide both chronic and acute timescale tools for reversible optogenetic inhibition, confirm fundamental predictions of the ion selectivity model

span.label: iC++ is named for the count of charges added, so the construct name encodes the mechanistic claim
span.quote: iC1C2 and iC++ are highly engineered (9 and 10 residues were replaced, respectively) variants of the cation-selective parental construct C1C2, with mutations chosen for the predicted ability to alter the electrostatic potential

span.label: extends → iC1C2, the first-generation structure-guided chloride-conducting channelrhodopsin
span.quote: Previous work showed that iC1C2 (engineered using a crystal structure-based electrostatic pore model) had higher chloride selectivity and conductivity at lower pH ( 8 ).

span.label: extends → the previously reported step-function variants SwiChR CA and SwiChR CT
span.quote: Step-function iC1C2 variants, denoted “SwiChR CA ” and “SwiChR CT ,” were reported previously ( 17 ), although the currents were low and efficacy was tested only in vitro.

span.label: builds-on → the naturally anion-conducting GtACR channelrhodopsins
span.quote: Strikingly, this model is validated further by the recently reported naturally anion-conducting Gt ACR channelrhodopsins ( 10 ), which contain amino acids at key positions within the ion pore equivalent to those in the earlier designed and reported iC1C2 and in iC++ ( 11 ).

span.label: builds-on → the structure-derived electrostatic model of channelrhodopsin pore selectivity
span.quote: The enhancements comprising iC++ support the model of channelrhodopsin selectivity ( 8 ) in which ions are selected primarily by electrostatic interactions between pore and ions.

span.label: confirms → the crystal structure-derived electrostatic model of channelrhodopsin pore selectivity
span.quote: The design and functional features of these next-generation chloride-conducting channelrhodopsins provide both chronic and acute timescale tools for reversible optogenetic inhibition, confirm fundamental predictions of the ion selectivity model

span.label: supports → the naturally occurring GtACR chloride channels, whose pore residues match the engineered ones
span.quote: Strikingly, this model is validated further by the recently reported naturally anion-conducting Gt ACR channelrhodopsins ( 10 ), which contain amino acids at key positions within the ion pore equivalent to those in the earlier designed and reported iC1C2 and in iC++

span.label: extends → the first-generation iC1C2 channel, which had small photocurrents and was never tested on behaviour
span.quote: Engineered channels indeed became chloride selective, reversing near −65 mV and enabling a new kind of optogenetic inhibition; however, these first-generation chloride-conducting channels displayed small photocurrents and were not tested for optogenetic inhibition of behavior.

span.label: qualifies → the use of light-activated chloride pumps for optogenetic inhibition
span.quote: Although optogenetic inhibitory pumps display more extreme V rev than the inhibitory channels described here, the pumps can hyperpolarize cells far beyond physiological levels, causing unstable membrane properties

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · shunting —contrasted-with→ hyperpolarization
span.quote: We observed that, because of stronger shunting, the chloride channel iC++ inhibited APs more efficiently than the chloride pump eNpHR3.0.

span.label: ion gradients —causes→ chloride
span.quote: In addition, microbial opsin pump currents will not show the influence of ion gradients reported here for channels; such gradients can differ across cell types, subcellular regions, developmental stages, and pathological states ( 12 – 15 , 30 ), even giving rise to excitation under some conditions.

span.label: electrostatic —causes→ chloride
span.quote: iC1C2 and iC++ are highly engineered (9 and 10 residues were replaced, respectively) variants of the cation-selective parental construct C1C2, with mutations chosen for the predicted ability to alter the electrostatic potential

span.label: channelrhodopsin —distinct-from→ pumps
span.quote: This effect can be reduced by lowering light intensity, although this strategy also severely reduces the volume of tissue inhibited by the pumps, which are less light sensitive than channels and, unlike the channels, cannot be converted to a more light-sensitive bistable step-function form.

span.label: reversal potential —operationalised-as→ chloride
span.quote: Engineered channels indeed became chloride selective, reversing near −65 mV and enabling a new kind of optogenetic inhibition; however, these first-generation chloride-conducting channels displayed small photocurrents and were not tested for optogenetic inhibition of behavior.

span.label: shunting —contrasted-with→ hyperpolarization
span.quote: We further show that inhibition by light-gated chloride channels is mediated mainly by shunting effects, which exert optogenetic control much more efficiently than the hyperpolarization induced by light-activated chloride pumps.

span.label: ANOVA (two-way repeated measures)
span.quote: Consistent with prior work ( 22 , 23 ), we observed robust avoidance of the light-paired compartment at multiple light intensities in all groups (two-way repeated-measures ANOVA, main effect of light power, F 2, 18 = 64.529, P < 0.001; Holm–Sidak post hoc tests, 0 mW vs. 0.5 or 5 mW, P < 0.005) ( Fig. 6 B and C ).

span.label: post hoc multiple comparison test (Holm-Sidak)
span.quote: Consistent with prior work ( 22 , 23 ), we observed robust avoidance of the light-paired compartment at multiple light intensities in all groups (two-way repeated-measures ANOVA, main effect of light power, F 2, 18 = 64.529, P < 0.001; Holm–Sidak post hoc tests, 0 mW vs. 0.5 or 5 mW, P < 0.005) ( Fig. 6 B and C ).

span.label: interaction effect in factorial ANOVA
span.quote: Optogenetic inhibition of vCREB neurons using iC++, iC1C2, or eNpHR3.0 significantly reduced tone-induced freezing, whereas silencing a similar number of neurons not overexpressing CREB had no effect [light (on, off) × virus ANOVA yielded a significant interaction, F 6,52 = 11.83, P < 0.001] ( Fig. 7 C ).

span.label: standard error of the mean
span.quote: Here, building from the iC++ backbone, we introduced the CA mutation C128A ( 8 ), which decelerated iC++ closure (τ off,fast = 12.1 ms ± 0.4 SEM) by 9,500-fold (resulting in SwiChR++ with τ off,dark = 115 s ± 9 SEM) ( Fig. 5 A – D ).

span.label: two-way repeated-measures ANOVA with Holm-Sidak post hoc
span.term: two-way repeated-measures ANOVA with Holm-Sidak post hoc
span.quote: Consistent with prior work ( 22 , 23 ), we observed robust avoidance of the light-paired compartment at multiple light intensities in all groups (two-way repeated-measures ANOVA, main effect of light power, F 2, 18 = 64.529, P < 0.001; Holm–Sidak post hoc tests, 0 mW vs. 0.5 or 5 mW, P < 0.005)

span.label: light by virus interaction ANOVA
span.quote: Optogenetic inhibition of vCREB neurons using iC++, iC1C2, or eNpHR3.0 significantly reduced tone-induced freezing, whereas silencing a similar number of neurons not overexpressing CREB had no effect [light (on, off) × virus ANOVA yielded a significant interaction, F 6,52 = 11.83, P < 0.001]

span.label: The paper tests and confirms that channelrhodopsin ion selectivity follows the electrostatic surface potential of the pore: negative pores pass cations, neutral-to-positive pores pass chloride.
span.quote: This paper tests the hypothesis that selectivity of channelrhodopsins is determined by surface potential of the pore region: Cations are conducted by a negatively charged pore, and chloride ions are conducted by a pore that has neutral and positively charged residues.

span.label: Structure-guided redesign produced iC++ and the bistable SwiChR++, with more than 15-fold larger photocurrents and a reversal potential about 15 mV more negative than the previous generation.
span.quote: Here we report the validation and further development of the channelrhodopsin pore model via crystal structure-guided engineering of next-generation light-activated chloride channels (iC++) and a bistable variant (SwiChR++) with net photocurrents increased more than 15-fold under physiological conditions, reversal potential further decreased by another ∼15 mV, inhibition of spiking faithfully tracking chloride gradients and intrinsic cell properties, strong expression in vivo, and the initial microbial opsin channel-inhibitor–based control of freely moving behavior.

span.label: Unlike its predecessor iC1C2, iC++ shows a reversal potential independent of the proton gradient, i.e. it does not conduct protons.
span.quote: Moreover, the V rev of iC++ was independent of the proton gradient, in contrast to iC1C2, indicating that iC++ does not conduct protons ( Fig. 3 G ).

span.label: iC++ passes other halides (iodide, bromide) but excludes physiological small organic anions.
span.quote: Additional characterization with ion-substitution experiments revealed that iC++ can conduct other anions, such as iodide and bromide, but not small organic anions that could be encountered in physiological systems, such as aspartate, bicarbonate, and gluconate ( SI Appendix , Fig. S2 ).

span.label: The purely model-driven engineered pore converged on the same residue solution that evolution produced in the natural anion channel GtACR2.
span.quote: This striking convergence reveals that the engineering of iC1C2 and iC++ for chloride conductance based entirely on the structure-derived model of electrostatic pore selectivity ( 7 , 8 ) resulted in a solution very similar to that arrived at by nature over the long timescales of evolution; the overall model for ion selectivity is consistent in both natural and engineered channelrhodopsins ( Fig. 2 ).

span.label: The chloride channel inhibited neurons far more efficiently than the chloride pump eNpHR3.0, blocking any tested input in over 90% of expressing cells.
span.quote: We found that light delivered to more than 90% of iC++-expressing cells could inhibit any current input tested; conversely, all the eNpHR3.0-expressing cells started to spike at some current amplitude under light ( SI Appendix , Fig. S7 D and E ).

span.label: A single C128A mutation on the iC++ backbone slowed channel closure by roughly four orders of magnitude, yielding a bistable tool switchable off by red light.
span.quote: SwiChR++ could be deactivated immediately by red light (τ off,600nm = 0.15 s ± 0.02 SEM), enabling temporally delimited bistable control over chloride conductance and neuronal inhibition ( Fig. 5 B and D ).

span.label: Inhibiting VTA dopamine neurons with iC++ produced real-time place aversion as effectively as the established pump opsins, the first behavioural control with a chloride-conducting channelrhodopsin.
span.quote: Under these experimental conditions, each opsin was equally effective in driving real-time place aversion (two-way repeated-measures ANOVA, no effect of group or group × light power interaction, P > 0.474).

span.label: Optogenetically silencing CREB-overexpressing amygdala neurons reduced tone-evoked freezing, while silencing an equal number of non-allocated neurons did not.
span.quote: Optogenetic inhibition of vCREB neurons using iC++, iC1C2, or eNpHR3.0 significantly reduced tone-induced freezing, whereas silencing a similar number of neurons not overexpressing CREB had no effect [light (on, off) × virus ANOVA yielded a significant interaction, F 6,52 = 11.83, P < 0.001] ( Fig. 7 C ).

span.label: net photocurrents increased more than 15-fold under physiological conditions
span.quote: Here we report the validation and further development of the channelrhodopsin pore model via crystal structure-guided engineering of next-generation light-activated chloride channels (iC++) and a bistable variant (SwiChR++) with net photocurrents increased more than 15-fold under physiological conditions, reversal potential further decreased by another ∼15 mV, inhibition of spiking faithfully tracking chloride gradients and intrinsic cell properties, strong expression in vivo, and the initial microbial opsin channel-inhibitor–based control of freely moving behavior.

span.label: effective photocurrent was more than 16 times larger than the first generation at comparable expression
span.quote: Protein expression levels of iC++ were comparable to those of iC1C2 ( SI Appendix , Fig. S2 ), but the effective photocurrent size of iC++ was more than 16 times larger ( Fig. 1 D ), whereas membrane properties of cells expressing iC++ remained comparable to those of eYFP-expressing cells

span.label: the advantage over the first generation is largest for short 5 ms pulses needing over 500 pA to drive spiking
span.quote: iC++ demonstrated a robust spike inhibition capability, with particular advantages over iC1C2 in the setting of short 5-ms pulse widths where strong current amplitudes of >500 pA were required to induce spiking

span.label: the engineered pore residues match those of a naturally occurring chloride channel discovered afterwards
span.quote: Interestingly, the newly discovered natural light-gated chloride channel Gt ACR2 ( 10 ) exhibits finely detailed similarity in predicted pore electrostatics to the iC1C2 and iC++ mutations ( Fig. 2 ), which were generated before knowledge of Gt ACR2 and in which specific side chains facing the pore are replaced by less polar or nonpolar residues, just as seen in Gt ACR2:

span.label: reverting one arginine to the wild-type histidine removed the leak current and restored input resistance
span.quote: Therefore we tested reversion of this arginine back to the histidine that is present in wild-type channelrhodopsins; as hypothesized (and as was consistent with our structural model), R134H increased R in and photocurrent size of the iC1C2-E83X mutations.

span.label: the channel inhibits spikes more efficiently than the chloride pump, through stronger shunting
span.quote: We observed that, because of stronger shunting, the chloride channel iC++ inhibited APs more efficiently than the chloride pump eNpHR3.0.

span.label: all three opsins produced equivalent real-time place aversion
span.quote: Under these experimental conditions, each opsin was equally effective in driving real-time place aversion (two-way repeated-measures ANOVA, no effect of group or group × light power interaction, P > 0.474).

span.label: silencing CREB-overexpressing amygdala neurons reduced fear freezing, while silencing the same number of non-CREB neurons did not
span.quote: whereas silencing a similar number of neurons not overexpressing CREB had no effect

span.label: the reduction in freezing did not differ significantly between the three opsins
span.quote: However, considering the baseline freezing when light was off, the reduction in freezing was not significantly different among the vCREB/iC++, vCREB/iC1C2, and vCREB/eNpHR3.0 groups ( P > 0.05).

span.label: channelrhodopsins
span.quote: Channelrhodopsins are membrane proteins that enable cellular regulation of transmembrane ion conductance through light-gated pores; these proteins have found application in optogenetics.

span.label: optogenetics
span.quote: Discovery and engineering of the microbial opsin genes not only has stimulated basic science investigation into the structure–function relationships of proteins involved in light-triggered ion flow but also has opened up opportunities for biological investigation (reviewed in ref. 1 ) via the technique of optogenetics, which involves targeting these genes and corresponding optical stimuli to control activity within specified types of cells within intact and functioning biological systems.

span.label: step-function opsin bistability
span.quote: One of the most useful properties of channel-type microbial opsins (compared with pumps) for optogenetics is the opportunity to create step-function opsin bistability ( 17 ), which allows orders-of-magnitude greater light sensitivity in expressing cells as well as lasting modulation without continuous light delivery ( 17 , 18 ).

span.label: optogenetics
span.quote: which involves targeting these genes and corresponding optical stimuli to control activity within specified types of cells within intact and functioning biological systems.

span.label: shunting inhibition, by analogy to GABA-A
span.term: shunting inhibition, by analogy to GABA-A
span.quote: through iC++ activation will reduce excitability, just as seen with endogenous chloride-conducting channels such as GABA A receptors, providing efficient inhibition via shunting of excitatory inputs

span.label: point mutations in the ion-conduction pathway
span.term: point mutations in the ion-conduction pathway
span.quote: To test this concept, we began by introducing a number of additional point mutations to iC1C2, specifically targeting residues in the ion-conduction pathway to enhance chloride flux guided by our model; reversal potential (V rev ) and photocurrent size were tracked for all variants ( Fig. 1 A – D ) in cultured hippocampal neurons using whole-cell patch-clamp recordings.

span.label: intracellular chloride concentration
span.quote: ( B and C ) V rev s ( B ) and photocurrents ( C ) of iC++ at the V AP (−52 ± 1 mV) measured for 5 s with light application under varying internal chloride concentrations ([Cl − ] int : 4, 12, and 20 mM).

span.label: external pH
span.quote: ( E ) pH-dependent photocurrents of iC1C2 and iC++ at neutral (black, pH ext 7.2) and acidic (red, pH ext 5.0) external pH values, pH int 7.2.

span.label: reversal potential (V rev)
span.quote: We systematically measured V rev with varying intracellular chloride concentrations ( Fig. 3 B and C ); the V rev of the peak and stationary currents closely matched the expected equilibrium potential under various chloride gradients, indicating the high chloride selectivity of the channel.

span.label: neuronal input resistance (R in)
span.quote: The largest shift in V rev was seen with E83 mutations, but these also drastically reduced neuronal input resistance (R in ) ( Fig. 1 C ), as was consistent with creation of a leak current.

span.label: fixed 12 mM internal chloride across cell types
span.term: fixed 12 mM internal chloride across cell types
span.quote: Internal chloride concentrations were kept equal (12 mM) to allow study of inhibition independent of varying chloride gradients.

span.label: eYFP-only expressing cells
span.quote: Cell membrane properties were not significantly different from those of control cells expressing only eYFP ( SI Appendix , Fig. S3 ).

span.label: reversal potential
span.quote: Engineered channels indeed became chloride selective, reversing near −65 mV and enabling a new kind of optogenetic inhibition; however, these first-generation chloride-conducting channels displayed small photocurrents and were not tested for optogenetic inhibition of behavior.

span.label: photocurrent amplitude
span.quote: Protein expression levels of iC++ were comparable to those of iC1C2 ( SI Appendix , Fig. S2 ), but the effective photocurrent size of iC++ was more than 16 times larger ( Fig. 1 D ), whereas membrane properties of cells expressing iC++ remained comparable to those of eYFP-expressing cells

span.label: time in the light-paired compartment
span.quote: Consistent with prior work ( 22 , 23 ), we observed robust avoidance of the light-paired compartment at multiple light intensities in all groups (two-way repeated-measures ANOVA, main effect of light power, F 2, 18 = 64.529, P < 0.001; Holm–Sidak post hoc tests, 0 mW vs. 0.5 or 5 mW, P < 0.005)

span.label: more than 16 times — increase in effective photocurrent size of iC++ over iC1C2 at comparable protein expression
span.quote: Protein expression levels of iC++ were comparable to those of iC1C2 ( SI Appendix , Fig. S2 ), but the effective photocurrent size of iC++ was more than 16 times larger ( Fig. 1 D ), whereas membrane properties of cells expressing iC++ remained comparable to those of eYFP-expressing cells ( SI Appendix , Fig. S2 ).

span.label: 9,500-fold (τ off,dark = 115 s ± 9) — slowing of channel closure produced by the C128A mutation, creating the bistable SwiChR++
span.quote: Here, building from the iC++ backbone, we introduced the CA mutation C128A ( 8 ), which decelerated iC++ closure (τ off,fast = 12.1 ms ± 0.4 SEM) by 9,500-fold (resulting in SwiChR++ with τ off,dark = 115 s ± 9 SEM) ( Fig. 5 A – D ).

span.label: 488 nm — peak activation wavelength of iC++, indicating an intact retinal-binding pocket
span.quote: The peak activation wavelength of iC++ was measured to be 488 nm ( SI Appendix , Fig. S2 ), suggesting that the properties of the retinal-binding pocket environment were maintained.

span.label: near −65 mV — reversal potential of the first-generation chloride-conducting channelrhodopsins
span.quote: Engineered channels indeed became chloride selective, reversing near −65 mV and enabling a new kind of optogenetic inhibition; however, these first-generation chloride-conducting channels displayed small photocurrents and were not tested for optogenetic inhibition of behavior.

span.label: 9 and 10 residues — number of amino acid replacements in iC1C2 and iC++ relative to the parental cation channel C1C2
span.quote: iC1C2 and iC++ are highly engineered (9 and 10 residues were replaced, respectively) variants of the cation-selective parental construct C1C2, with mutations chosen for the predicted ability to alter the electrostatic potential of the ion-conducting pore from predominantly negative to predominantly positive ( 7 , 8 , 11 ).

span.label: at least seven times — efficiency advantage of the iC++ channel over the eNpHR3.0 pump in inhibiting current-driven spiking
span.quote: Moreover, eNpHR3.0-expressing cells could inhibit only responses to input currents that were equal to the magnitude of eNpHR3.0 photocurrent; in contrast, iC++-expressing cells were at least seven times more efficient and exhibited a prominent light-induced reduction in R in ( SI Appendix , Fig. S7 F ).

span.label: more than 90% — proportion of iC++-expressing cells in which light blocked every current input tested
span.quote: We found that light delivered to more than 90% of iC++-expressing cells could inhibit any current input tested; conversely, all the eNpHR3.0-expressing cells started to spike at some current amplitude under light ( SI Appendix , Fig. S7 D and E ).

span.label: ∼15% — share of lateral amygdala pyramidal neurons transduced before fear conditioning in the memory-engram experiment
span.quote: We used viral vectors expressing vCREB and iC++, vCREB and iC1C2, or vCREB and eNpHR3.0 (or each inhibitory opsin on its own) to transduce a small portion (∼15%) of the LA pyramidal neurons before fear conditioning and tested mice in both the presence and absence of light.

span.label: more than 15-fold, and more than 16 times at matched expression — photocurrent improvement over the first generation
span.quote: Protein expression levels of iC++ were comparable to those of iC1C2 ( SI Appendix , Fig. S2 ), but the effective photocurrent size of iC++ was more than 16 times larger ( Fig. 1 D ), whereas membrane properties of cells expressing iC++ remained comparable to those of eYFP-expressing cells

span.quote: Engineered channels indeed became chloride selective, reversing near −65 mV and enabling a new kind of optogenetic inhibition; however, these first-generation chloride-conducting channels displayed small photocurrents and were not tested for optogenetic inhibition of behavior.

span.label: 9 and 10 residues replaced — how heavily engineered the two constructs are
span.quote: iC1C2 and iC++ are highly engineered (9 and 10 residues were replaced, respectively) variants of the cation-selective parental construct C1C2, with mutations chosen for the predicted ability to alter the electrostatic potential

span.quote: Optogenetic inhibition of vCREB neurons using iC++, iC1C2, or eNpHR3.0 significantly reduced tone-induced freezing, whereas silencing a similar number of neurons not overexpressing CREB had no effect [light (on, off) × virus ANOVA yielded a significant interaction, F 6,52 = 11.83, P < 0.001]
